title: fxv error payload
description: Payload schema emitted under a message kind of `error` when a command fails. Any command can produce this payload instead of its own; the process exit code is carried in `exit_code`.

message.description: Human readable description of the failure - the same text the human output format prints to stderr.

exit_code.description: The process exit code the CLI returns for this failure. 1 is a general error; 98 means a previous sync was interrupted and the workspace must be recovered with `fxv resume`; 99 means the workspace was locked by another process.

backtrace.description: Backtrace captured at the point the error was raised. Present only when backtrace capture was enabled (e.g. RUST_BACKTRACE=1) and a backtrace was available.

error_data.description: Machine-readable detail for failures that have some, so a consumer can act without parsing `message`. Absent for most errors.

errorData.description: Mirrors the message envelope's kind/version/payload triple, so each error's detail shape is dispatched on and versioned the same way as a top-level message and independently of this envelope.

kind.description: Identifies the payload's shape, and therefore which schema describes it. `interrupted-sync` is described by urn:fxv:schema:interrupted-sync:v1.

version.description: The payload's own major.minor schema version, independent of the error envelope's.

payload.description: The detail itself; its shape is determined by `kind`.
